text:
Adam Pelech has played his whole career for the Islanders, more than 650 games, and he's the kind of defenseman whose value hides in the numbers most people don't look at. Evolving-Hockey's adjusted model had him driving play (89th percentile) and taking chances away (95th percentile) last season, and noted he was better than his goals. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him stopping 19% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%.

This season the on-ice results haven't matched that reputation: the Islanders have taken 41% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 14 points worse than without him. Part of that is role. With Ryan Pulock out, he and Logan Stanley have carried the penalty kill on some nights, and Stefen Rosner noted at least one shift where Pelech never got to sit down.

He has three points in 16 games, including an overtime winner against Minnesota. Our range says 11 to 24 points over a full season. Nobody plays him for points. If the Islanders get healthy, his minutes get easier and his five-on-five numbers should come back toward his career norm.
headline: Pelech carries the hard minutes
